newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips rebound at close, small caps strong.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips rebound at close, small caps strong.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip stocks staged a rebound in late afternoon trading as foreign institutional funds bought select large-capitalised issues.

The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed up 2.04 points to 1,239.54, while the Second Board index of small-capitalised stocks continued its rise, closing up 5.09 to 617.69.

"Foreign funds have been buying Rashid Hussain, Tenaga, Gamuda, IJM and Sime Darby today. So even though the index is up the buying has been very stock specific," said an institutional dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage house.
"There's also a switch by punters from Second Board stocks to second-liner main board stocks," said the dealer.
Mycom closed down 16 cents to 3.58 after its 54.7 percent-owned subsidiary Olympia Industries had the renewal of its gaming licence disallowed by the east Malaysian Sabah state government.

Rashid Hussain was up 30 to 18.20 ringgit, while Maybank was down 75 cents to 26.25. "Institutional investors are switching out of Maybank into Rashid Hussain. They feel they only need to be exposed to one major finance play which has strong growth potential," said the dealer.
